sections.h2: Who sends the Galveston tax statement
sections.html:
One bill comes from the Galveston County Tax Office, which collects for the city, Galveston ISD, Galveston College and the county. Most island owners get one statement covering several taxing units, and every dollar goes to a local unit rather than the state.

Two offices matter. The Galveston Central Appraisal District sets each parcel's market value as of January 1 and decides exemption claims. Its customer service desk takes mail at 9850 Emmett F. Lowry Expressway, Suite A101, Texas City, Texas 77591, and the phone is (409) 935-1980. The tax office collects the money, takes mail at 722 21st Street, Galveston, TX 77550, and answers balance questions at (409) 766-2481.

Only the appraisal district can change ownership or the mailing address on a parcel. The tax office will pass a correction along as a courtesy, but a seller who moved or a buyer who just closed should file the change with the appraisal district so the next statement reaches the right person.

City Council approved the FY2027 budget on September 18, 2026, with a 2026 rate of $0.416273 per $100 of property value. The city describes that figure as the no-new-revenue rate, meaning the rate that raises the same revenue as the prior year from properties taxed in both years.

The budget sets operating funds at about $250.1 million and adds a five-year capital plan of roughly $347.8 million. Its fiscal year starts October 1.

The city's rate is one piece of the bill. Galveston ISD, the county, Galveston College and any special district such as a waterway or drainage district each adopt their own rate. The appraisal district lists every unit that taxes a given parcel on its property page, and the Texas.gov property tax database shows proposed and adopted rates during late summer.

sections.h2: Due dates, penalties and payment plans
sections.html:
Expect the statement in October and pay before January ends. A postmark after January 31 means penalties, and anything open on February 1 is delinquent, unless you use one of the plans below.

The day after the deadline, a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest attach. From there the penalty adds a point each month, reaching 12 percent on July 1, while interest keeps building monthly with no cap. A collection attorney hired by the unit may add another charge, capped at 20 percent. A written waiver request goes to the county's Penalty and Interest Committee, and waivers are allowed in limited cases if the owner pays within 21 days of finding out the tax is delinquent.

Galveston County Tax Office payment choices
Payment optionRule
Single paymentDue by January 31, delinquent February 1
Split paymentFirst half by November 30, second half by June 30
Quarterly installmentsFour equal payments, due at the end of January, March, May and July, for homesteads of seniors, disabled persons, disabled-veteran owners and their spouses
Payment agreementCall to set one up; it can head off attorney fees added July 1
Advance paymentPay early and write ESCROW in the subject line with the account number

Paying online by e-check or card adds a processing fee. You can also pay by phone at 1-800-420-1663 or leave a payment in the yellow drop box at any full-time office. Mail payments to the 722 21st Street address, because the postal service does not always recognize the Moody Avenue address.

Start with the homestead exemption, which the appraisal district offers to owners who live in the house. Apply by mail, online or in person, and expect a decision within 90 days of receipt. The general filing deadline is before May 1.

  • Galveston ISD taxes a homestead on $140,000 less than its value, and owners over 65 or disabled see another $60,000 come off the school tax base.
  • Some units add an optional percentage exemption, up to 20 percent of value but never below $5,000.
  • Seniors and disabled owners keep a school tax ceiling even after moving to another Texas homestead. A widow or widower aged 55 or older can hold on to it.
  • A disabled-veteran owner's exemption grows with the VA rating, and at 100 percent it can wipe out the homestead tax.

With the exemption in place, appraised value on a homestead is held to a 10 percent yearly rise. A protest of value is due May 15, or 30 days after delivery of a late notice. The county tax office also carries a tax deferral affidavit (state form 50-126) for owners who qualify.

Galveston has held steady in size: 53,636 people in the July 2025 estimate against 53,695 in 2020, on 41.05 square miles of land. Owners live in 46.2 percent of housing units, which leaves most to renters. A middle-of-the-range owner-occupied home is worth $326,000, with monthly rent near $1,298. Residents 65 or older make up 20.9 percent, the group that qualifies for the school tax ceiling and quarterly installments.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell a Galveston house
sections.html:
Island properties often carry storm-related repairs, short-term tenants or mixed ownership, and each of those can slow a sale if the tax record is unclear. Clear the tax question first and the rest becomes simpler.

Bring a short packet to your first talk with a buyer or title officer: the most recent tax statement, your homestead exemption approval if you have one, and the name of any mortgage servicer that pays taxes through escrow. If you recently moved, confirm the appraisal district has your current mailing address.

Next, phone (409) 766-2481 and request a payoff that stays good through the day you expect to close. With a cash sale there is typically no lender appraisal or repair list, which leaves the tax payoff as the main item to schedule.

Selling does not erase a tax debt. Each January 1 a lien secures that year's tax on the parcel, and whoever owned it that day stays liable after any later transfer.

Pull a current statement from the county tax office before you list. Find out too whether your mortgage servicer already paid the bill from escrow. A mortgage code only appears after a lender requests the statement, so sign up for e-statements in the first year after a payoff or refinance so the bill is not missed.

  • Back taxes, penalties and interest usually come out of your proceeds at the closing table.
  • If you never had the homestead exemption, the buyer can still claim it for the rest of the year after a closing past January 1.
  • An owner who cannot cover the bill may ask about a payment agreement, available after February 1, before deciding to sell.

Owing back taxes, needing storm repairs or having tenants in place need not block an as-is sale to a cash buyer. Keep the payoff letter. It lets the closing statement show the tax paid and the lien lifted.

faqs.q: Where does the money go when I pay tax on a Galveston house?
faqs.a: The Galveston County Tax Office collects for the city, Galveston ISD, the county and several other units on one statement, then passes each unit its share. Statements arrive in October.

faqs.q: What rate did the City of Galveston set for 2026?
faqs.a: $0.416273 per $100 of value, set with the FY2027 budget on September 18, 2026. Your full rate is the sum of the school, county and special district rates.

faqs.q: Can I split my Galveston property tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying half by November 30 leaves the second half open until June 30, with no penalty or interest. Senior, disabled and disabled-veteran homesteads can choose four installments instead, due at the end of January, March, May and July.

faqs.q: What is the homestead application deadline?
faqs.a: Send your application to the appraisal district ahead of May 1 in the tax year it should apply. The district acts within 90 days of receiving the application and will tell you if you do not qualify.

faqs.q: Does a sale make a tax lien on my Galveston house disappear?
faqs.a: No. The parcel carries the lien until the balance is paid. Request a payoff statement from the county tax office, and the title company can pay it from your proceeds.
